title: The .oai files are NIS-Elements Segment.ai training snapshots — the masks are NOT inside them
body: Each .oai is a tagged binary (UTF-16BE keys) holding a training config header, `umnet_v3_0` U-Net weights with batchnorm running stats, and full Adam optimizer state (per-tensor means and vars) — a resumable training checkpoint. That is why all three are ~84.33 MB regardless of how big the paired image is. The config carries a `skipBinary` key and *references* its training data by path (`trainFileNames`); no ground-truth raster is embedded. The masks the user drew live as **binary layers inside the ND2 files themselves**, which `nd2.ND2File.binary_data` reads directly.
why: Reroutes the 'read the embedded masks' task: nothing needs to parse 84 MB of .oai — the GT comes out of the ND2s in three lines of python. The .oai files are still valuable as provenance: they say exactly which channel (`inputNames`) and which layer (`outputNames`) the lab's previous NIS.ai model was trained on, i.e. what the CellSAM model is supposed to replace.

rows: EMP_..._Focused EDF Document.nd2 (in folder) + PrEC_..._crop_crop_crop - binary_1.nd2 (MISSING)
evidence.caption: Training config recovered from each .oai header. Note the cross-references: the PrEC-named model was trained on the EMP image, and the EMP model's second training file (the PrEC mask carrier) is not in H:/HK_segmentation.

rows: zoom, inputMetadata (modality/excitation/emission/color), lr, epochs, batchSize, blur, rotations, flips, noise, gamma, numCascades, size, skipBinary, trainFileNames, inputNames, outputNames
umnet_v3_0 conv/batchnorm tensors + adam_opt:mean/var per tensor

title: Two of three ND2s carry INSTANCE-labelled hand segmentations; the third has none
body: `nd2.ND2File.binary_data` decodes each NIS binary layer to a uint16 **label image** — per-object ids, not a flat binary. 2025 ND2 (750x850): layer 'Binary from ROI', 45 objects, ids 1..45. EMP ND2 (2048x2048): layer 'HomogeneousSegmentation', 306 objects, ids 1..306. PrEC ND2 (2048x2048): **no binary layer at all**. No two labels touch anywhere (0 adjacent different-label pixel pairs) — neighbouring cells are separated by a background gap, so even binarisation would not merge them. All four channels are DAPI / GFP / AF555 / AF647 at 0.1901 um/px; images are EDF (single-plane) documents. Oddities: 9/45 and 54/306 labels consist of more than one connected piece, and the 2025 layer has two 1-px slivers. The standalone Mask.tif agrees with the embedded 2025 layer on only 32.3% of pixels — it is NOT that mask (possibly a colocalization product); excluded from GT.
why: Instance labels are exactly what CellSAM evaluation and fine-tuning need — the binary-to-instance conversion problem never arises. Current GT: 351 cells across 2 fields, median cell 245 um2 (2025) / 354 um2 (EMP), equivalent diameter ~18-21 um, dense confluent monolayers (69% / 85% coverage). Only 2 objects sit under CellSAM's hard 25-px floor (both 1-px slivers, almost certainly junk).

evidence.caption: Per-field GT audit. Multi-part = labels whose pixels form >1 connected component.

images.caption: 2025 field. Look at panel 3/4: boundaries are smooth hand-drawn strokes that follow whole-cell outlines on AF647 — clearly manual. Check whether any cell visible in panel 1 lacks an outline (annotation exhaustiveness).

EMP field. Boundaries hug cells tightly but the zoom shows ragged pixel-level edges — the signature of MODEL OUTPUT (layer name 'HomogeneousSegmentation'), possibly hand-corrected. Compare with the smooth strokes in the 2025 overlay. Provenance question pending (e-ask).

Per-object areas, log scale. Both fields are unimodal around 200-400 um2; the red dashed line is CellSAM's non-negotiable 25-px (0.90 um2) lower floor — only the two 1-px slivers fall under it, so the floor costs nothing here.

note: User: 'Keep that retracted.' The claim 'hand segmentations' is withdrawn for the EMP field - 'HomogeneousSegmentation' is only potentially hand-drawn, so it is NOT manual GT until confirmed. The extraction mechanics (instance labels via nd2.binary_data) remain valid and are re-stated in the GT-freeze entry. GT = the 2025 field only.

title: Everything needed to test CellSAM on this GT is already installed and on disk
body: The repo ships CellSAM inference glue (nodegraph/kernels/cellsam_segment.py) behind `analysis.segment` method=cellsam. Both published checkpoints are on disk. Torch has CUDA on an RTX 3090. Critically, the node already has a `model_path` socket that loads any local .pt via `cellSAM.get_local_model` — so a fine-tuned checkpoint integrates with ZERO engine changes. Precedent: ~/.deepcell/models already holds a custom fine-tuned Cellpose .pt from earlier lab work.
why: Phase A (zero-shot baseline) can run immediately; integration of a fine-tuned model is drop-in.

title: Plan: freeze GT, measure zero-shot CellSAM honestly, fine-tune only if the gate fails
body:
P0 GT LOCK-IN - resolve the pending asks (PrEC mask, EMP provenance, fragments), then freeze GT as label TIFFs + a provenance JSON (source file, layer name, channel, um/px) so every later score points at an immutable input.
P1 ZERO-SHOT BASELINE - run cellsam_general AND cellsam_extra on the AF647 plane of each GT field (one process per checkpoint). Score: instance F1 across IoU 0.5-0.9, boundary error in um (IoU alone hides a boundary a full radius out on 20-um cells), false-split/false-merge counts. Log per-field overlays of predicted vs GT boundaries for the user's eye.
P2 THRESHOLD CALIBRATION - sweep bbox_threshold x mask_threshold x mask_quality, leave-one-field-out; widen any range whose winner lands on an edge; report out-of-sample only.
P3 DECISION GATE (user) - if calibrated zero-shot meets the agreed gate, ship the thresholds as a recipe and stop: no training, no new weights to maintain.
P4 FINE-TUNE (only if P3 fails) - on the 3090. P1's diagnostics choose the surgery: boundary errors -> fine-tune the SAM mask decoder (GT boxes as prompts, dice+focal); detection misses -> CellFinder needs the work (harder; upstream ships no training code - budget for writing it). Hold out a whole field, never cells. Deliverable: a local .pt for the existing model_path socket.
P5 INTEGRATION - recipe + gates + docs; every default cites the evidence entry that set it.
why: Zero-shot-first is the cheap path: if threshold calibration alone reaches the gate, the lab gets a model with no training pipeline to maintain. And with only 2-3 GT fields, every fitted number is fragile - leave-one-field-out is the only honest split, and any conclusion is provisional until more fields are annotated (the labelling-sheet and hand-drawing tools in this skill are ready if we need to grow GT).

evidence.text: **Metric blindness, stated up front:** instance F1 at IoU 0.5 cannot see boundary placement on large cells; boundary error cannot see missed cells; neither sees whether per-cell INTENSITY (the likely real product, given 'Count_Intensity_Colocalization' in the filename) is right. If the gate is intensity-driven, P1 adds a per-cell intensity agreement check (GT-mask vs predicted-mask AF555/GFP means).

**GT caveat carried into every score:** the GT gaps between touching cells (no two labels adjacent anywhere) mean CellSAM's un-gapped boundaries will show a systematic ~1 px 'error' at every shared edge; scoring will either add the same gap to predictions (remove_boundaries=True) or report the offset separately, not blame the model for it.

title: Four GT questions before the ground truth is frozen
body:
(a) The PrEC ND2 has NO embedded mask. The EMP .oai references 'PrEC_1-5_EMP_6-10_col_3kp_7d_..._crop_crop_crop - binary_1.nd2' (hkhawaja's Documents) as its second training file - that file is not in H:/HK_segmentation.
(b) The EMP layer is named 'HomogeneousSegmentation' and its edges are ragged pixel-level (see the EMP overlay zoom), unlike the smooth hand strokes of the 2025 field - it looks like MODEL OUTPUT, possibly hand-corrected.
(c) The standalone Mask.tif matches the embedded 2025 mask on only 32.3% of pixels.
(d) 9/45 (2025) and 54/306 (EMP) labels are multi-piece, and 2025 has two 1-px slivers.
why: (a) decides whether GT is 351 cells on 2 fields or ~650 on 3 - with N this small, a third field roughly halves the fragility of every cross-validated number. (b) decides whether the EMP field counts as MANUAL ground truth at all; training a model on another model's uncorrected output would launder its errors into ours. (c)/(d) decide what gets dropped before freezing.
asks: (a) Can you locate or re-export the PrEC mask (NIS: open the PrEC ND2, if its binary layer exists elsewhere save it into an ND2/TIFF)? (b) Was 'HomogeneousSegmentation' drawn by hand, model output that WAS hand-corrected, or raw model output? (c) What is Mask.tif (colocalization mask? different layer?) - OK to exclude from GT? (d) Multi-piece labels: real fragmented cells, or drawing artefacts - and may I drop the two 1-px slivers?
note: User: 2025 field is definitely hand-drawn; EMP/PrEC only POTENTIALLY hand-drawn - more files arrive later; focus on 2025 for now; drop the 1-px slivers; verify mask fidelity to its file. Done in this batch: GT frozen from the 2025 layer (see gt entry).

title: Define the model's input and the success gate
body: The lab's NIS.ai models took AF647 (one also took AF555) as input and produced whole-cell masks. CellSAM will be baselined the same way: single AF647 plane in the whole-cell slot. Options beyond that exist (DAPI+AF647 two-channel fusion is a real CellSAM capability but is deliberately not exposed by the node yet - it would need a Label-domain channel-key decision).
why: The gate decides P3: whether calibrated zero-shot is 'done' or fine-tuning starts. A gate must be checkable by a metric we can compute against your masks, and the metric must see the thing you actually care about - counts, boundaries, or per-cell intensities (the filename 'Count_Intensity_Colocalization' suggests intensities are the real product).
asks: (1) Confirm AF647 as the model input (or tell me the channel you segment by eye). (2) What is the downstream product - cell counts, boundaries for morphology, or per-cell intensity/colocalization? (3) Proposed gate, adjust as needed: on a held-out field, instance F1@IoU0.5 >= 0.85 AND median boundary error <= 1 um (~5 px); add per-cell intensity agreement if (2) says intensities. (4) Confirm this stays academic/non-commercial (CellSAM weights license).
note: User: input = AF647; downstream product = cell segmentation itself (boundaries) - other nodes handle measurement; academic/non-commercial confirmed; ALSO test the DAPI+AF647 two-channel fusion alongside single-channel.

title: Ground truth frozen: 43 hand-drawn cells from the 2025 field (2 slivers dropped)
body: gt_2025_labels.tif (uint16, contiguous ids) + gt_2025_provenance.json written under this investigation. Dropped 1-px sliver ids [33]; kept every multi-piece label and the small-but-real labels [(34, 2)] (id, px). Fidelity checks: mask shape equals the image plane (750x850) - True; layer name matches the 2025.oai outputNames ('Binary from ROI'); the .oai inputNames says the annotation was drawn against AF647; pixel size 0.1901 um/px from the file metadata, not assumed.

title: Fibro_test.tif, all four methods at raw node defaults: only the learned methods produce cells
body: One 1024x1024 GFP frame of dense fibroblasts (1.7183 um/px, 12-bit, from the ImageJ metadata). Each method ran through the REAL analysis.segment node with untouched defaults. threshold (otsu) outlines only the bright cores and speckle - median object 6 um2 is noise, not cells. watershed shatters the same foreground into 8085 fragments. stardist finds 1699 cell-shaped objects (median 505 um2) but its star-convex prior visibly clips the long thin fibroblast tails. cellsam finds 1121 objects (median 1261 um2) covering bright AND dim cells, but boundaries are rounded and inflated - in the zoom several outlines enclose background or swallow a dim neighbour. Learned-method timings include their one-off model load (StarDist: TF is CPU-only on native Windows; CellSAM ran on the 3090).
why: This is why no single default exists yet: the two classical methods need per-dataset tuning (level / min_distance) to mean anything here, and the two learned methods disagree with each other by 2.5x on median cell area. WHAT THIS COMPARISON IS BLIND TO: there is no ground truth for this file, so counts and medians describe BEHAVIOUR, not accuracy - nothing here says which method is right. Scoring needs labels: either a quick labelling sheet on sampled tiles, or hand-drawn boundaries on a crop (both tools are ready).

evidence.caption: All four at node defaults on the same frame. CellSAM's shipped mask_threshold=0.4 (paper says 0.5) inflates mask extent - one candidate explanation for the 1261 um2 median; the sweep will test it.

images.caption: Top: full frame; bottom: the same zoom for every method. Look at the zoom row: threshold hugs only bright cores; watershed dices them; stardist truncates elongated tails into rounded blobs; cellsam covers dim cells the others miss but draws inflated oval boundaries that sometimes take in background or a neighbour.

title: Next: score CellSAM against the frozen 2025 GT; fusion and single-cell deep dive queued
body:
1) ZERO-SHOT SCORING on gt_2025_labels.tif: cellsam_general and cellsam_extra (separate processes - one model pull per process), AF647 plane; instance F1 across IoU 0.5-0.9, boundary error in um, split/merge counts; then the 3-threshold sweep. The GT's 1-px inter-cell gaps get mirrored in predictions (remove_boundaries=True) so the gap is not scored as model error.
2) TWO-CHANNEL FUSION (user-requested): same scoring with DAPI in the nuclear slot + AF647 in the whole-cell slot, via the kernel/cellSAM directly - the node deliberately does not expose fusion yet; if fusion wins clearly, a node design decision (Label-domain channel key) goes through build-node-v2.
3) SINGLE-CELL DEEP DIVE (user-requested): per-cell tiles of the bright cells and the multi-piece labels in the 2025 field; and a fragment-to-parent association method - candidate signals: gap distance, intensity continuity along the connecting path, and boundary curvature agreement - evaluated against the 7 kept multi-piece GT labels, not tuned to one example.
why: Order matters: scoring zero-shot on real GT tells us whether fine-tuning is needed at all before anyone invests in a training pipeline; fusion is the cheapest possibly-large accuracy lever; the deep dive answers the user's standing question about brightness and fragments with per-cell evidence.

title: Zero-shot CellSAM on the frozen 44-cell GT: F1@0.5 climbs 0.77 -> 0.85; fusion is the biggest lever
body: All runs on the 2025 field (AF647; fusion adds DAPI in the nuclear slot), remove_boundaries=True so CellSAM gets the same 1-px inter-cell gap convention the GT uses. Baselines ran through the REAL analysis.segment node; sweeps through the kernel after proving the two routes agree to the pixel (1.0 agreement at defaults, both checkpoints). Sweep grids were widened until every winner was interior: extra's best quality moved 0.7 -> 0.8 with 0.9 tested and worse; general's bbox 0.6 has 0.5 and 0.7 both tested and worse. The three thresholds are WEAK levers here: across 60 configs the whole F1@0.5 surface spans only 0.74-0.81 (extra) / 0.71-0.78 (general). Two-channel fusion moves more than any knob: +0.03 over the best single-channel. Boundary error on matched cells is already sub-micron everywhere (0.77-0.93 um median vs the proposed 1 um gate).
why: cellsam_extra dominates cellsam_general on this data, tuning helps but cannot close the gap alone, and the DAPI+AF647 fusion - which the node deliberately does not expose yet - is where the accuracy is. BLINDNESS: one field, 44 cells, in-sample (the sweep optimised on the same field it reports); one cell changes F1 by ~0.02; fusion used thresholds tuned for single-channel (not separately swept, some protection against overfit but same-field). Nothing here is out-of-sample until more annotated fields exist.

evidence.caption: The ladder. Note mask_threshold=0.5 (the paper's value, not the shipped 0.4) appears in every winning config - the shipped default inflates masks on this data too.

images.caption: GT green vs prediction red, same zoom for all three panels. Look at how closely red tracks green on most cells in the fusion panel, and at the top-left zoom cell where single-channel merges two dim cells that fusion separates (the DAPI nuclei disambiguate them).
F1 vs match strictness. All curves fall steeply past IoU 0.75 - boundaries agree at the 'same cell' level but not at the 'same pixels' level. The dashed line is the proposed F1@0.5 gate.

title: Fusion-best residuals: only TWO real misses; most 'false positives' look like unannotated cells
body: The 0.845 decomposes as TP 41, FN 3, FP 12. Of the 3 misses: GT id 33 is the 2-px fragment kept at freeze time (old id 34) - physically unfindable below CellSAM's 25-px floor and almost certainly not a cell; ids 4 and 22 are real misses (id 4 looks like a partial-cell annotation; id 22 is a clear round cell CellSAM skipped). Of the 12 unmatched predictions, several (17, 35, 42, 51 at least) outline plausible, well-formed cells that simply have no green counterpart - if the 2025 annotation is not exhaustive, these are CORRECT detections scored as errors, and the true F1 is higher than 0.845.
why: Whether zero-shot fusion already clears the 0.85 gate hinges on the user's eye, not on more computation: judging 12 tiles takes two minutes and could add several TPs. This is also the cheapest possible demonstration of why annotation exhaustiveness (or a scored-region rectangle) matters for every future field.

images.caption: Green: the 3 'missed' GT cells (note id 33 is a 2-px speck). Red: all 12 unmatched predictions. For each red tile ask: would you have drawn this cell? A yes converts that FP into a TP.

The number is probably an UNDERestimate if any red tile in the residual gallery is a real cell you would have drawn.

title: Labelling sheet ready: 22 tiles, ~3 minutes

body: Joined against the blind manifest. CONTROLS: 8 of 9 labelled 'y' - and the ninth is a real discovery: control pred 45 (823 um2, the largest object) got 'm' - a genuine merge that IoU-matching had silently accepted as a TP. A border-exclusion policy plus any min_area >= 1 um2 removes all four remaining FPs - both are standard, honest scoring rules worth adopting for every future field. User's boundary verdict stands over all of it: 90-95% correct but never perfectly flush to the fluorescence - the systematic sub-micron offset (median 0.767 um) that sharper input or decoder fine-tuning would attack.

BLINDNESS: the adjudication looked at model proposals (a prompted eye can accept borderline objects), though 8/9 control consistency plus the caught merge argue the labels were not rubber-stamped; still one field, still in-sample. Out-of-sample confirmation waits on the incoming annotated files.

title: ZS-DeconvNet auto-fill formula - and beta1/beta2 are NOISE-MODEL params, not Adam betas
body:
THE CATCH FIRST: on enhance.zs_deconvnet, beta1/beta2 parameterize the re-corruption noise model (estimated variance = beta1 x (intensity - background) + beta2): beta1 = camera gain in ADU per electron (shot-noise scale), beta2 = read-noise variance in counts squared. The Adam optimizer's betas are fixed inside the kernel at published values and are not sockets. Filling 0.9/0.999 here would silently mis-model the camera.

THE FORMULA (prototype: zs_autofill_prototype.py; filled values: zs_params_filled.json): emission_nm and na read straight from ND2 metadata; background = ~1st percentile of the channel (pedestal); beta1 from the camera's gain, beta2 = (read_noise_e x beta1)^2, both measurable by photon transfer or dark frames when specs are unknown; train_units = min(8, planes available); iterations = time_budget / t_step with t_step CALIBRATED by a ~50-step run - TensorFlow is CPU-only on native Windows, so the paper's 50k-on-GPU is not a reachable reference point; everything else keeps the node's published-value defaults (lr 5e-5, batch 4, patch 128, denoise 0.5, hess 0.02, upsample on).

FILLED: HK 2025 AF647 -> emission 655 nm, NA 0.8, background 42, beta defaults (AX camera, unmeasured), train_units 1 - the file has ONE 750x850 plane, which is thin material for self-supervised training. Monolayer_stain Red -> emission 600 nm, NA 0.75, background 94, beta1 1.18 / beta2 2.0 (Kinetix spec ballpark), train_units 8 from 160 planes - far better training material. Note the Monolayer data is ~2x undersampled (PSF sigma ~0.17 um vs 0.325 um pixels), so upsample=True is doing real work there.
why: This is the requested 'formula of best applications': every socket now has a stated metadata or measurement source, which is what wiring it into the node as metadata-aware auto-fill (via build-node-v2, like emission_nm's existing resolution rule) needs. The two beta values are the only sockets that cannot be derived from theory - they are camera properties.

evidence.caption: Auto-fill formula with both datasets filled. TBD = needs the 50-step timing calibration before the 9h run is sized.

title: Before the 9h training run: three decisions
body: The parameter sets are filled (zs_params_filled.json). What the formula cannot decide alone: (a) WHICH dataset the 9h run trains on - the Monolayer Red stack is the strong candidate (160 planes, measured pedestal, Kinetix specs); the HK 2025 file has a single small plane and would make a weak self-supervised teacher. (b) ITERATIONS: TensorFlow runs CPU-only on native Windows here, so I should time ~50 steps first and size iterations to fit 9 hours honestly - say the word and I run that calibration now. (c) beta1/beta2 for the AX camera (HK file) are unmeasured defaults; if you can give me two back-to-back identical exposures or a dark frame from that scope, I measure them properly.
why: A 9h run sized against GPU-paper numbers would quietly train a fraction of the intended steps; a run on the 1-plane HK file would spend 9h on thin data. After training, the queued test closes the loop: segment the ZS-enhanced AF647 with the fusion config and re-score against GT v2 - the packed-boundary weakness is exactly what sharper input should move.
asks: (a) 9h run on Monolayer Red, the HK field, or both? (b) Run the 50-step timing calibration now? (c) Can you provide dark/replicate frames for the AX camera, or do we accept beta defaults for the HK file?
note: User: push raw-input segmentation to maximum GT fidelity first (no ZS-DeconvNet), run ~9h ZS-DeconvNet training, then segment the deconvolved version with the best raw parameters and deliver the comparison - autonomously, self-corrected against GT. Mid-turn: 'Run the 50-step calibration now.' All three done/underway below.

title: Calibration: 1.37 s/iteration on this CPU - the 9h budget buys 23,000 steps
body: Timed the real node (enhance.zs_deconvnet, zero_shot, 2D, formula params) on the HK AF647 plane: 10 iters = 62.4 s, 60 iters = 128.6 s, 300 iters = 458.9 s -> slope 1.32-1.37 s/step, setup ~49 s. Matches the node doc's measured ~1.4 s (TensorFlow is CPU-only on native Windows). 9 h / 1.37 s = ~23,000 iterations (paper reference: 50,000 on an RTX 3090 in ~1 h). One scare, resolved: the 10-iteration output was ALL ZEROS - an untrained net flattened by output percentile normalization, not an extraction bug; at 300 iterations the output is a clean denoised (not yet sharpened) version of the input at the 2x grid (1500x1700, 0.0951 um/px), see figure.
why: Sizing iterations by the paper's GPU numbers would have promised 50k steps and delivered a third of them. 23,000 steps in ~8.8 h is what this machine can honestly do; whether that is enough sharpening for the packed-boundary problem is exactly what the comparison will show.

images.caption: Same region, raw AF647 vs the 300-iteration checkpoint (2x grid). Speckle is gone, structure preserved, no artifacts - and no sharpening yet, which is expected this early. The green light for the long run.

title: Raw-input ceiling: corrected F1 = 0.990 at bbox 0.3 / mask 0.5 / quality 0.8 - boundary error is input-limited
body: Fine fusion sweep (DAPI+AF647, cellsam_extra) scored with the labels-corrected metric adopted from e019: amnesty for the 8 user-confirmed unannotated cells (IoU>=0.5 against their footprints), border-touching and sub-1-um2 unmatched preds excluded (user-verified artifact classes). Best config: TP 41 + 8 amnesty, FN 1 (cell id 22, the one confirmed miss), ZERO residual false positives, 1 merge, boundary median 0.767 um. The optimum is interior in every direction after extending the grid both ways: bbox 0.25 -> 0.970 and 0.2 -> 0.961 (extra low-confidence detections become real FPs), bbox 0.4 -> lower, mask/quality neighbours all lower. Notably the boundary median never moved off ~0.77 um across the entire grid - the flushness deficit the user described is a property of the INPUT resolution/blur, not of any threshold.
why: This is the raw-file ceiling the user asked for: detection is essentially solved (one miss, one merge in ~50 cells); boundary flushness is the remaining axis and no knob reaches it. METRIC HONESTY: the corrected metric embeds amnesty footprints taken from one fusion run's predictions - a mild circularity risk; mitigations: the footprints are frozen, the border/speck rules are objective, and the final comparison will report plain F1-vs-GT alongside. Still one field, in-sample.

evidence.caption: The bbox axis at mask 0.5 / quality 0.8. Interior optimum at 0.3; boundary median ~0.77 um everywhere.

title: 9h ZS-DeconvNet training LAUNCHED: 23,000 iterations on the HK AF647 plane
body: Background process started (task bx3hd9fkv): enhance.zs_deconvnet, zero_shot, 2D, 23,000 iterations, formula params (emission 655 nm, NA 0.8, background 42, beta1 1.0, beta2 0.0, lr 5e-5, batch 4, patch 128, upsample on). Model cached to cache/zs_hk2025_af647*, enhanced plane to cache/zs_hk2025_af647_23k.tif (1500x1700 @ 0.0951 um/px). ETA ~8.8 h. WHEN IT LANDS, the comparison runs without user input: segment the deconvolved AF647 (fused with 2x-upsampled raw DAPI) using the raw-best config, score in GT space, compare against the raw ceiling - plus a tiled variant, since CellSAM's internal 1024 resize would otherwise throw away most of the 2x upsampling on a 1700-px frame.
why: The single-plane caveat stands (train_units=1: one 750x850 plane is thin self-supervised material - flagged in e020) - this run is the user-directed experiment to test exactly that. The betas are AX-camera defaults; if the comparison disappoints, measured betas (dark frames) are the first suspect.

title: 23,000-iteration ZS-DeconvNet training completed: 8.4 h wall, model cached
body: Background run finished cleanly (30,260 s = 1.31 s/step, matching the calibration). Artifacts: cache/zs_hk2025_af647_c0.weights.h5 (52.6 MB, reusable via cache_path or weights_path) + zs_hk2025_af647_23k.tif (1500x1700 @ 0.0951 um/px). Visual read of the output (progression figure): edges visibly tighter than raw, noise gone - and a fine STIPPLE texture across the frame, a known deconvolution artifact class consistent with thin training data (one 750x850 plane, train_units=1) and unmeasured camera betas. Recorded, not hidden: it did not stop the segmentation gains below, but measured betas + more training material are the obvious first fixes if this preprocessing is adopted.
why: The model is permanent - any rerun of this enhancement is now ~2 min of inference, not 8 h.

images.caption: Same region: raw -> 300 iter (denoise only) -> 23,000 iter (deconvolved, 2x grid). Look at the bright cell's rim tightening left to right, and at the fine stipple in the right panel - the artifact to watch.

title: Verdict: deconvolved input fixes every structural error (0 miss / 0 merge / 0 split) and ties the raw ceiling at F1c 0.990; boundary agreement vs raw-anchored GT is worse
body: Fusion segmentation (DAPI + deconvolved AF647) at the 2x grid, best config bbox 0.4 / mask 0.5 / quality 0.8, scored in GT space: corrected F1 = 0.9899 - identical to the raw ceiling - but the error PROFILE is strictly cleaner: FN 0 (it finds GT cell 22, the raw config's one miss - see the zoom), merges 0 (raw: 1), splits 0, one residual FP. Plain F1@0.5 is higher than raw (0.884 vs 0.854). The flip side: boundary median 0.842 um vs raw's 0.767, and F1@0.75 drops to 0.59 from 0.69 - the deconvolved boundaries sit systematically INSIDE the hand-drawn ones. Two readings, both logged: (a) the sharpening genuinely misplaces boundaries; (b) the GT was drawn on the BLURRY raw image, so its outlines are dilated by the PSF and a tighter boundary gets punished even where it is more faithful to the actual cell edge. This metric cannot distinguish (a) from (b) - only a human judging boundaries on the sharpened image can. The 1x-grid variant (deconv averaged back to the raw grid) scores 0.969 - the 2x resolution is part of the detection gain, exactly the user's intuition on e010.
why: The user's directive is fulfilled: raw ceiling, 9h training, comparison. What detection needed, deconvolution delivered - every count-level error on this field is now gone or amnestied. What remains is a BOUNDARY ANCHOR question, not a segmentation question: which outline is 'right', the one drawn on raw or the one the sharpened image implies? BLINDNESS: same field the model trained on (self-supervised - no labels leaked, but the enhancement is tuned to this noise/blur), amnesty metric shared with e023, still in-sample.

evidence.caption: The comparison the 9h run bought. Detection: deconv wins outright. Boundary-vs-GT: raw wins - but the GT itself is anchored to the raw blur (see body).

images.caption: Same GT (green) for both. Zoom row: GT cell 22 - the raw run's fragmented double-contour miss (left) becomes one clean cell (right). Also visible on the right: red sitting slightly inside green on many cells - the boundary-anchor question in one image.

title: The boundary-anchor question - and whether to adopt deconvolution preprocessing
body: Deconvolved input eliminated every miss, merge and split on this field. The only metric it 'lost' is agreement with boundaries that were drawn on the blurry raw image. Before adopting deconv+fusion as the recipe, one judgment only you can make: on the sharpened image, are the tighter boundaries MORE faithful to the real cell edges you see, or has the deconvolution eaten into the cells?
why: If the tighter boundaries are right, the recipe becomes zs_deconvnet -> segment(fusion) and future GT should be drawn on enhanced images; if they are wrong, we keep raw for boundaries and use deconv only to rescue detection. Everything downstream (the recipe default, the deep-dive targets, how the new annotated files get scored) forks on this.
asks: (1) I can build a hand-drawing ground-truth page (the gt tool) showing the SHARPENED image for ~6 cells so you draw what you see there - the drawn-on-sharp vs drawn-on-raw offset then settles (a)-vs-(b) with numbers. Want it? (2) Meanwhile: adopt deconv+fusion as the candidate recipe, or hold until the new annotated files arrive for an out-of-sample check?
